text:
nina: Quick sync - observed ambiguity in lease/ownership semantics for tenant bindings across hosted/dedicated/private. Two production surprises in canary: duplicate lease issuance and unclear telemetry attribution when a lease moves. Need a small, opinionated contract.

paul: Saw the dup lease too. Sequence was: hosted issued lease L1, then a rebind created L2 on Private while L1 was still valid; both accepted writes for a short period. We need a single source-of-truth "lease-holder" and clear idempotency rules.

emma: Suggest canonical fields on the handshake manifest: lease_id (opaque), lease_holder (hosted|dedicated|private), lease_ttl_seconds, lease_epoch (monotonic), lease_mode (exclusive|shared). Runtime enforces exclusive by default.

nina: Example snippet to discuss:
```yaml
handshake:
  flow: hosted->private
  lease_id: "le-3b7f"
  lease_mode: exclusive
  lease_ttl_seconds: 45
  lease_epoch: 7
  audit: minimal
```

paul: Behavior rules idea: 1) idempotent bind: re-applying same lease_id+epoch is a no-op; 2) new epoch increments lease_epoch and invalidates previous epoch for writes; reads can be served for lease_ttl_seconds if lease_mode==exclusive but must include X-Lease-Epoch header; 3) on epoch mismatch writes return 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED with error `lease_epoch_mismatch`.

emma: That maps nicely to our cache_epoch ideas but focused on ownership. Also add lease_transfer intent: if a host wants to hand off gracefully, it sends intent=transfer and runtime moves through TRANSFER_PENDING -> TRANSFER_ACTIVE -> TRANSFER_COMMIT. If target refuses, runtime rolls back. Expose metrics lease_transfer_latency.

telemetry-bot: telemetry-bot: canary "lease-transfer-probe" executed on runtime-staging at 08:22 UTC :white_check_mark:

paul: Telemetry: avoid embedding tenant ids in lease payloads. Lease should carry only an opaque lease_label and a MACed mapping that only telemetry sidecars can unwrap for billing/attribution. E.g. lease_token: {label:"l-abc", mac:"..."}. Hosted sees label only.

nina: Agreed. Also we need mapping for cost attribution when a fallback uses a service_account: include orig_tenant_label (opaque) in logs but encrypted. Telemetry sidecar performs attribution.

emma: SDK ergonomics: runtime-client should expose a LeaseHandle object with methods: acquire(), renew(), release(), on_epoch_change(callback). It should surface 412 errors as LeaseEpochError and optionally auto-renew+rebind if configured. Keep default conservative (auto-renew=false).

paul: Edgecases: what if two nodes race to acquire exclusive lease? Runtime should use compare-and-swap on epoch and return a deterministic winner; loser receives lease_conflict with suggested backoff and a recommended retry_after seconds equal to jittered fraction of lease_ttl_seconds. Document exponential backoff + jitter.

nina: Auditing: emit events: lease.request, lease.granted(lease_label,holder,epoch), lease.revoked(reason), lease.transfer.initiated, lease.transfer.completed, lease.conflict. Include correlation_id but not plaintext tenant id in event; include tenant_label only.

runtime-bot: runtime-bot: note added to staging canary: enforce `lease_mode=exclusive` default and emit `lease_epoch_mismatch` 412 for mismatched epochs.

emma: Action items: nina will add a small RFC appendix defining lease fields and default semantics; paul will draft SDK LeaseHandle prototype and error types; i'll wire telemetry sidecar opaque-unwrapping flow and the audit event shapes. We'll keep defaults conservative: lease_ttl_seconds=30-60s, lease_mode=exclusive, auto-renew disabled.

paul: One more: add a short test matrix for canary: (1) concurrent acquire race, (2) graceful transfer, (3) sudden revoke, (4) fallback to service_account with opaque label mapping. We'll run those tomorrow.

nina: Great. If we keep lease semantics narrow and explicit we can avoid a lot of cross-mode surprises. Thanks all :thumbsup:
